evidence: Receiving online DO2 at t=52.0h: 9.94 mg/L; minimum over all receiving DO2 records ~7.05 mg/L (t=26.6h) — far above the 2.0 mg/L limit
Receiving delayed assays: P=1.006 g/L @36h (avail 40h), P=2.892 g/L @48h (avail 52h), consistent with source-batch trajectory (source-1: 1.117 @36h, 3.057 @48h)
Physics tool (nominal, source-calibrated): keep → 576 kg product, min DO 6.52 mg/L, zero oxygen deficit; all 5 sensitivity members feasible (min DO 4.04–7.42)
Physics tool reduce_feed → 596 kg, min DO 7.34; marginal gain only in a nominal model not calibrated to the receiving process
submission.rationale: The receiving fermentation is tracking the source-batch trajectory normally: P at 48h is 2.89 g/L (vs 3.0–3.1 g/L in the three source batches at the same age), and DO2 is 9.94 mg/L at the 52h decision time with a historical minimum of ~7.1 mg/L — far above the 2.0 mg/L oxygen limit. The nominal forward model confirms KEEP is feasible (min DO 6.5 mg/L, zero oxygen deficit, ~576 kg product; all sensitivity members feasible). reduce_feed shows a marginal nominal mass gain (596 kg) but the model is source-calibrated and imperfect; DO is not stressed, so there is no evidence-based need to intervene. Unnecessary feed reduction risks yield loss and deviating from the validated source trajectory. No extra assay is needed: DO2 shows no stress and the latest P assay (48h) already confirms normal production.
submission.uncertainty: Moderate: the receiving process parameters differ from source and hidden states are unobservable; the DO2 downward drift from ~14 to ~7 mg/L over 0–28h mirrors source behavior and stabilized, so no oxygen-constraint violation is expected (predicted post-decision min DO 6.5 mg/L, sensitivity floor 4.0 mg/L). If the model misestimates receiving oxygen demand, DO could fall below 2 mg/L late in the run; however observed receiving DO is uniformly higher than source at matched times, arguing against this. Marginal nominal advantage of reduce_feed (~3%) is within model calibration error and carries yield risk.
